declarations.docstring: For a nonzero polynomial, the degree-zero value on its principal quotient and the polynomial module has at most one element.
Finite modules over a polynomial ring admit simultaneous descriptions of the first two degrees by products of quotient modules, while every degree from two onward is subsingleton.
For a finite module over a polynomial ring, the value in every degree at least two against an arbitrary module object is subsingleton.
The degree-zero value from the polynomial module to a module object is additively equivalent to the carrier of that object.
Under the stated nonvanishing condition, the degree-one value is additively equivalent to an indexed family of quotients by ideals generated by two displayed polynomials.
Under the two stated nonvanishing conditions, the degree-zero value is additively equivalent to a product of a finite power and an indexed family of two-generator quotients.
Linear maps from the quotient by a nonzero principal polynomial ideal to the polynomial ring form a subsingleton.
